thesis.text: What does the Church–Turing thesis say?

every-problem.text: A Turing machine can solve every problem
every-problem.why: Lessons 4 and 5 show problems that no machine can solve. The thesis is about methods that a person can follow.

person-and-machine.text: What a person can compute by following a fixed method, a Turing machine can compute
person-and-machine.why: That is the thesis. It links a method that a person follows with a machine.

speed.text: A Turing machine computes faster than a person
speed.why: The thesis says nothing about speed. It is about what can be computed at all.

why-thesis.text: Why is it a thesis and not a theorem?

believed-false.why: That is not the reason. A theorem needs a proof, and a proof needs exact definitions.

proof-too-long.text: Because its proof is too long to write down
proof-too-long.why: No proof exists, long or short. One side of the claim has no exact definition.

no-exact-definition.text: Because “a fixed method that a person can follow” has no exact definition, so no proof can link it to Turing machines
no-exact-definition.why: Turing says so on page 249: all arguments for it are, in the end, appeals to intuition.

same-sequences.text: That the λ-definable sequences and the computable sequences are the same
same-sequences.why: Turing proves both directions, in outline, on pages 263 to 265.

church-wrong.why: Turing calls Church’s idea equivalent to his own (page 231).

thesis-proved.why: It shows that two exact definitions agree. The idea of a method that a person can follow still has no exact definition.

circle-free-machine.text: When a circle-free machine prints it
circle-free-machine.why: That is Turing’s definition of a computable sequence (page 233). The appendix shows that both give the same sequences, but the definitions differ.

one-formula.text: When one formula of Church gives every figure of it, by conversion
one-formula.why: Apply the formula to the number n and convert. The result names the n-th figure (page 263).

no-rule.text: When its figures follow no rule
no-rule.why: Both definitions need fixed rules. A sequence with no rule is neither λ-definable nor computable.

no-method.text: Turing proved that no machine decides, for every formula, whether it is provable. What turns this into “no method at all”?

more-steps.text: Running the machine for more steps
more-steps.why: More steps do not help. The question is whether every method can be carried out by a machine.

appendix-alone.why: The appendix compares two exact definitions. It does not cover every method that a person might follow.

thesis.text: The thesis: every fixed method can be carried out by a machine
thesis.why: Turing says this on page 249. Once the thesis is granted, a method for the Entscheidungsproblem would be a machine, and no such machine exists.
